subject: Maths
title: Rotation
subtitle: Transformations · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can rotate shapes about a given centre by 90, 180, or 270 degrees.

key_vocab.definition: A rotation turns a shape around a fixed point called the centre of rotation. You need to know the centre, angle, and direction (clockwise or anticlockwise).

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can rotate shapes about a given centre by 90, 180, or 270 degrees.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: rotation -- A rotation turns a shape around a fixed point called the centre of rotation. You need to know the centre, angle, and direction (clockwise or anticlockwise).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
To describe a rotation, state: centre, angle, and direction. The shape does not change size.
90° CW about O: (x, y) → (y, -x)
180°: (x, y) → (-x, -y)

Key examples:
  ✓ (3, 1) rotated 90° clockwise about origin = (1, -3)  ((x,y)→(y,-x))
  ✓ (3, 1) rotated 180° about origin = (-3, -1)  (negate both)
  ✓ Rotation preserves shape and size  (congruent image)
  ✗ 90° clockwise is the same as 90° anticlockwise  (they are opposite directions)
  ✗ Rotation changes the size of the shape  (size is preserved)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – 90 clockwise about origin
  Rotate (2, 5) by 90° clockwise about (0, 0).
  Rule: (x, y) → (y, -x)
  (2, 5) → (5, -2)
  Image is at (5, -2)
  (5, -2)
  (Swap coordinates and negate the new y.)

Example 2 – 180 about origin
  Rotate (3, -1) by 180° about (0, 0).
  Rule: (x, y) → (-x, -y)
  (3, -1) → (-3, 1)
  Image is at (-3, 1)
  (-3, 1)
  (Negate both coordinates.)

sections.title: About a non-origin centre
sections.content:
Rotate 180° about the given centre.

(a) (4, 3) about (2, 2)
(b) (5, 1) about (3, 3)
(c) (1, 4) about (3, 2)
(d) (6, 5) about (4, 3)

sections.title: Mixed rotations
sections.content:
Perform each rotation.

(a) (3, 1) 90° CW about origin
(b) (2, 4) 180° about origin
(c) (1, 5) 90° ACW about origin
(d) (4, 2) 90° CW about (2, 1)
(e) (1, 3) 180° about (2, 2)

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ 180° rotation about origin: (x,y) becomes (-x,-y)
✗ 90° clockwise and 90° anticlockwise give the same image
✓ Rotation preserves the shape and size
✗ A 360° rotation returns the shape to a different position
✓ The centre of rotation does not move

teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

90° clockwise about origin:
  (a) (3, -1)
  (b) (2, -4)
  (c) (5, 1)
  (d) (4, 0)

180° about origin:
  (a) (-3, -2)
  (b) (1, -4)
  (c) (-5, 3)
  (d) (2, 6)

90° anticlockwise about origin:
  (a) (-3, 2)
  (b) (-1, 5)
  (c) (-4, -3)
  (d) (0, 6)

About a non-origin centre:
  (a) (0, 1)
  (b) (1, 5)
  (c) (5, 0)
  (d) (2, 1)

Mixed rotations:
  (a) (1, -3)
  (b) (-2, -4)
  (c) (-5, 1)
  (d) (3, -1)
  (e) (3, 1)
